clue.text: Weapon for Grace Darling, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a cosh or bludgeon, the old name for a short weighted club
Grace Darling was the lighthouse keeper's daughter famed for rowing out to save shipwrecked sailors in 1838

explanation.surface: Someone asks what weapon the heroine Grace Darling might have carried.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Darling is a Victorian British heroine who rescued survivors of the Forfarshire wreck; she is an example of someone who kept people alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a weighted club used as a weapon and, literally, one who saves lives, which Grace Darling did.

clue.text: Had Cupid nothing to do with this flower?

definitions.text: Had Cupid nothing to do with this flower?

parts.words: Had Cupid nothing to do with this flower?
parts.note: if the god of desire were idle, desire itself would be unoccupied, which is the old country name of a pansy

explanation.walkthrough: The old name for the wild pansy appears in A Midsummer Night's Dream as the flower struck by Cupid's arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the folk name of the wild pansy, heartsease, used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Composer represents: the whole Soccer organization?

annotationWithheld.why: Composer represents: the whole Soccer organization? (5): FALLA is ALL (the whole) inside FA (Soccer organization), but as held no word signals the containment
annotationWithheld.clue: Composer represents: the whole Soccer organization?

clue.text: West Yorkshire town makes agreement about reform of rent

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

indicators.note: reform means the letters of of rent are reshaped

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire town strikes a deal over changes to rents.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a dispute over rents; Pontefract is a historic market town known for liquorice.
explanation.definitionFit: A town near Wakefield famous for its liquorice cakes lies in the West Riding.

clue.text: Animals follow direction — a good thing one might say

definitions.text: a good thing one might say

indicators.note: follow says the animals are placed after the direction

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
a pig is a farm animal
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Beasts are herded one way, which is a clever thing to remark.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Animals', supplies two separate beasts, and 'a good thing one might say' is the definition rather than praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy witty saying is a neat remark worth repeating.

clue.text: Time for composition in G flat first?-

indicators.note: first places the level word at the front of the answer

parts.note: flat means even, level
G is a musical note, fitting the surface of a piece of music

explanation.surface: A piece of music to be written in G-flat, first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G flat' looks like a key signature, but 'flat' means level and is moved to the front by 'first'; the definition is a loose, playful one, the hours when writers settle to compose.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet hours after the working day are a traditional period for writing or composing music.

clue.text: Only man's description of hymn?

parts.note: Heber's hymn From Greenland's Icy Mountains says every prospect pleases and only man is the wicked word

explanation.walkthrough: The line from Reginald Heber's missionary hymn runs 'Where every prospect pleases, And only man is vile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hymn calls mankind wicked and base, the single word it applies to men alone.

clue.text: Move back from the tee — Corder is out of form

indicators.note: out of form means the letters of tee and Corder lose their shape and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer steps back from the tee because his partner is playing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is golf, but 'out of form' rearranges TEE and CORDER; 'from the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede again, going backwards, or to cede territory back, is a formal verb for retreating.

clue.text: Staggeringly abandoned?

parts.note: a lurch is a stagger, so being deserted can be read as being dropped mid-stagger

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deserted in a difficult spot, and a lurch is also a staggering movement.

clue.text: Saint enveloped by love?

definitions.meaning: the third-century martyr whose feast falls on 14 February
a romantic card posted in an envelope, sent out of affection

explanation.surface: A holy man is wrapped up in love.
explanation.definitionFit: The martyr gives his name to the February card, which is sealed in an envelope and sent from fondness.

clue.text: Turner read articles after start of Lent

indicators.note: start of tells us to take only the opening letter of the word Lent

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The painter Turner reads some essays once Lent begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J. M. W. Turner, but it means a machine that turns wood or metal; 'read' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine tool that spins the work so it can be shaped is something that turns.

clue.text: Angry demand for change of air before half-term

indicators.note: a call for a change asks for the letters of air to be rearranged
half picks out the first two of the four letters of term

explanation.surface: An angry pupil wants fresh air before the half-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging AIR gives IRA, and the front half of 'term' gives TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious or cross is the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Bar for travellers?

definitions.meaning: a horizontal rod or bar, as on a fence or towel holder
the railway, the track trains run along

explanation.surface: A pub built for those on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is one sense; the other is the track of a railway, used by passengers who go by train.

clue.text: Mount went shooting off

definitions.meaning: a horse to ride, here a young male horse
a revolver, named after Samuel ..., makes a gun go off

explanation.surface: A rider's horse bolted at the sound of the guns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colt is the famous American revolver, so the second half describes what one does when fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A young stallion can be ridden, and the Colt firearm is a brand of revolver used for shooting.

clue.text: Irish river polluted ?

definitions.meaning: a river in Munster flowing out at Youghal
dirty, dark liquid, as a stream fouled by pollution might be

explanation.surface: A river in Ireland has been contaminated.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a river in southern Ireland, and literally describes dark, dirty waterway liquid.

clue.text: Meanwhile, one enters during work period

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a school or university term is a period of work
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In the meantime someone starts work during the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meanwhile' is an adverb, while the answer is mostly a noun or adjective; 'in the interim' is the bridge that makes the swap fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the time between two events, a stopgap period.

clue.text: It displays the bill of fare

definitions.text: It displays the bill of fare

parts.words: It displays the bill of fare
parts.note: a bill of fare is usually a menu, but here fare is what a cab passenger pays

explanation.definitionFit: The cab's meter shows the passenger's charge for the journey.

clue.text: Many in' storm on ship

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind, a storm
all stands loosely for many, everyone

explanation.surface: Lots of people out in a storm aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall sailing vessel of the Spanish treasure fleets is a kind of ship.

clue.text: Meaningful work

parts.note: read literally, a book full of meanings, which is what a dictionary is

explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is a reference book that lists the meanings of words.

clue.text: I am seen wandering in the plant

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of I am seen stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted roaming through the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is a flower; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a South African garden flower grown as a bedding annual.

clue.text: Regicide and scholar with a stake In the church

parts.note: MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: In means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
a stake is a bet, a wager

explanation.surface: A king-killer and a scholar wager in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Scottish thane murdered King Duncan, so he is a regicide, a killer of a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's thane kills King Duncan to take the throne, which makes him a king-murderer.

clue.text: Sid confounded in reward for an evil act

indicators.note: in means the mixed letters go inside the other word

parts.note: meed is an old word for reward

indicators.note: confounded means the letters of Sid are mixed up

explanation.surface: Sid is baffled at being repaid for doing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' turns SID into ISD, placed in MEED, an archaic word for a deserved reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong or wicked deed is a misdeed.

clue.text: Address companion

parts.note: on forms the item always paired with one's address is what one is called

explanation.definitionFit: Forms ask for these two together, so one is the partner of where you live.

clue.text: Birds are found in them, usually

indicators.note: are found in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on where birds normally live.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flightless Australian runners are birds.

clue.text: Revolver for the modern highwayman?

parts.note: the old highwayman carried a pistol; today's man on the highway, the motorist, holds the round steering control that turns

explanation.definitionFit: The steering control a driver grips is round and turns, so it revolves.

clue.text: Taken in (of course)

parts.note: taken in suggests deceived, but a course is part of a meal, so it means swallowed

explanation.definitionFit: A dish that has been consumed has been swallowed down.

clue.text: On the right, .a rising river

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: To the right, a river climbs upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the run ONRA backwards. The answer is the river through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan waterway through Florence is a river.

clue.text: " Hyperion to a" (Hamlet)

parts.note: Hamlet compares his dead father to his uncle as the sun god is to a goatish woodland creature

explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet Act 1 Scene 2 the prince says his father was, to Claudius, 'Hyperion to a' half-man, half-goat; the clue asks you to finish the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word of Hamlet's line is the lustful goat-legged woodland deity of Greek myth.

clue.text: The periodical on the stand?

definitions.meaning: the long-running London weekly magazine of politics and culture
someone watching from the grandstand at a match

explanation.surface: A magazine displayed on the newsstand.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a British weekly and the word for an onlooker in the stands at a sporting event.

clue.text: To do barn repair stock farm thoroughly

indicators.note: repair means the letters of to do barn are fixed into a new order

parts.note: a ranch is a farm raising livestock

explanation.surface: A farmer plans to fix the barn on a cattle farm properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The farm in the surface misleads: 'stock farm' is a single piece, while 'To do barn' is the rearranged material.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely, down to the roots and out to every branch.
